sections.heading: C — Traffic Control Device Categories and Pavement Markings
sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic Control Device Categories and Pavement Markings

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
Traffic flow is controlled by pavement markings, traffic islands, signals and signs, and these devices fall into three categories, regulatory devices, warning devices, and guide and information signs [A01].
Why it matters: the three-category framework organizes the whole chapter.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Regulatory devices tell you to stop, to go a certain direction or to limit your speed, every regulatory device demands an action from you, and failing to comply is subject to penalty [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
Warning devices advise you of hazardous conditions or the possibility of them, and ignoring a warning device can lead to a crash caused by your own negligence [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
Guide and information signs help you find your way safely or give information that makes the trip more comfortable [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
Pavement markings are lines, words or figures placed on the pavement with paint, reflectors or other markers, and yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions [A01].
Why it matters: yellow means opposing traffic is on the other side; white means same-direction traffic.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A01
A single broken yellow centerline marks a road with only two lanes of traffic, you drive to its right, and you may cross it to pass another vehicle when it is safe [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A01
Double solid yellow lines mark the center of a road where passing is prohibited in both directions, and you may cross them only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A01
A no passing line is a single solid yellow line on a two-lane road marking a zone where passing is prohibited, and like the double yellow line it may be crossed only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road or driveway [A01].
Why it matters: the left-turn exception applies to both the single and the double solid yellow line.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A02
White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and you are required to drive between them [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A02
A single dashed white lane line may be crossed whenever you can do so safely [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A02
A single solid white line warns that changing lanes there is hazardous, a wider line signals a greater hazard, and such a line may be crossed only in unusual circumstances and only with great care [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A03
A double solid white line means that moving from lane to lane is prohibited, and you must not cross it [A03].
Why it matters: single solid white may be crossed with great care; double solid white may never be crossed.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A03
Red pavement markings or red reflectors mark a roadway that must not be entered or used [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A03
Edge lines are solid white or yellow lines along the edge of the roadway used as a safety guide, with white along the right edge and yellow allowed along the left edge of divided streets and highways [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A04
A stop line is a solid white line running across the lanes at an intersection or pedestrian crosswalk, and it shows exactly where to stop [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A04
Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to cross safely and warn drivers that pedestrians may be crossing at that spot, and you must stop for pedestrians in crosswalks [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A04
Two-way left turn channelization markings combine solid and dashed yellow lines to mark a center lane that vehicles traveling in either direction may use only for left turns, and the lane must never be used for passing [A04].
Why it matters: the shared center lane is for turning only, never for passing or through travel.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A05
Obstruction markings are solid lines in the traffic lanes, yellow or white, that steer you around an obstruction in the road such as a bridge support [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A05
White obstruction markings may be passed on either side, but yellow obstruction markings must be kept on your left, so you pass them on the right only [A05].
Why it matters: yellow keeps you to the right because opposing traffic is on the other side of it.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A05
Directional markings are white arrows or words painted in the lane to show the direction you must take, you must move only as the arrow indicates, and where arrows show more than one direction you may choose any of them [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A06
Railroad crossing markings are white markings in the traffic lane before a crossing, consisting of a large X with two R letters, a solid yellow centerline running the whole distance to prevent passing, and a white stop line across the lane [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A06
Traffic islands come in many designs, from painted markings alone to combinations of curbing, paving or landscaping, and they are used to direct you into separate traffic lanes [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A06
A traffic island is called a safety island when it protects pedestrians who may have to stand in the roadway, and you should never drive into or across a traffic island [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0038]

Misconceptions: a single solid white line may be crossed in unusual circumstances with great care, but a double solid white line may never be crossed; double yellow lines may be crossed to turn left into a driveway or alley even though passing across them is prohibited; the shared center left-turn lane is never a passing lane; yellow obstruction markings must be passed on the right only, while white ones may be passed on either side; a broken yellow centerline allows passing only when it is safe, not whenever it is present.

Mnemonics: Yellow divides opposite traffic, white divides same-direction traffic; broken means cross when safe, single solid means hazard, double solid means never; left turns into driveways are the one exception to solid yellow.

Glossary: regulatory device (a sign, signal or marking that requires an action, enforced by penalty); warning device (a device that advises of a hazard); centerline (the line separating opposing traffic, always yellow); edge line (a solid line along the pavement edge used as a guide); channelization markings (lines that assign a lane to a particular movement, such as the two-way left turn lane); safety island (a traffic island that shelters pedestrians).

Dynamic facts: none; marking colors, patterns and their meanings are national conventions printed as stable knowledge in this edition.

items.why: the chapter pairs each marking with a diagram, and the knowledge test covers traffic control devices, so a learner must identify a marking from its color, pattern and position and state what it permits

corpus_stability.reason: The Hawaii Driver's Manual is a periodically reprinted reference (imprint HMG 5/2023, copyright line through 2023); the the three categories of traffic control devices and the meaning of yellow and white centerlines, lane lines, edge lines, stop and crosswalk lines, two-way left turn lanes, obstruction, directional and railroad markings, and traffic islands rules on pages 33–38 are statutory and procedural content that changes less than once a year, so no BlockedProbe.
